packs.title: Landmarks & Living City
packs.promise: Make your own discoveries at Philadelphia’s defining stops.

q.s: Discover the market through ingredients rather than rankings.
st: Enter through an open public market entrance and choose a short aisle that leaves room for shoppers.
Find three ingredients or food types displayed by different vendors. Read signs from the customer side; do not ask for free samples.
Build an imaginary meal from those three discoveries and explain which combination surprised you. A purchase is optional.

q.s: Choose what an arrival looks like for you.
st: Begin this chapter at the museum’s east-side steps. Choose the base, an accessible permitted viewpoint or a stair ascent that suits you; running is unnecessary.
Frame the steps or the Parkway as a setting for your own small accomplishment. You do not need to pose or include yourself.
Give the image or written scene a short title celebrating something you actually did today.

q.s: Follow the river from a path that leaves the bank.
st: Arrive at an open signed Schuylkill Banks access point and use the official trail map to reach the boardwalk. Choose an out-and-back distance that suits you.
At a safe pull-off or resting point, compare how close the river feels on the boardwalk with the view from land.
Record one change in reflected light, passing movement or the angle of the riverbank before turning back or continuing to an open exit.

packs.title: Old City in Detail
packs.promise: Read small streets, open outlines and familiar landmarks with fresh eyes.

q.s: Find the repeated marks that hold a small facade together.
st: Return to 2nd Street and follow the sidewalk south to Arch, then west toward 239 Arch Street.
From the public sidewalk, find three repeated details in the exterior: a brick joint, a window division and a roof or trim rhythm.
Record them as three different imaginary stitches. Give each a short name without claiming it is a historic sewing technique.

q.t: A Steeple in a Small Frame
q.s: Make a tall landmark fit into a very small composition.
st: Follow Arch east to 2nd, then south toward Church Street. Find a comfortable public-sidewalk view of the church.
Frame the steeple with one nearby roofline or street detail, keeping private windows and people out.
Write a six-word caption that describes looking up from this particular block.

q.s: Notice how a short walk changes the scale of a city.
st: From the Liberty Bell area, use marked crossings to reach 5th and Walnut. Follow Walnut east to 3rd Street, then turn south toward Spruce.
At two comfortable stopping points, compare the size of a doorway, the width of the sidewalk and the distance between street trees or lamps.
Choose the moment the street began to feel different. Record the visible change that caused it, then continue west on Spruce toward Washington Square.
